;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[August 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Thirteen people are killed and two others injured after two bombs explode in [[Spin Boldak District|Spin Boldak]], [[Kandahar Province|Kandahar]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/blasts-kandahar-kill-13-civilians-official (TOLOnews)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador]]
***The [[International Monetary Fund]] reaches an agreement with the [[government of Ecuador]] to lend [[United States dollar|$]]6.5 billion to help fund [[Economy of Ecuador|the country's economy]] amid the pandemic and the subsequent fall in oil prices and finalize a [[debt restructuring]] deal with its international investors. [https://www.ft.com/content/fe14a91e-a72a-439d-8ac0-bf7f0d9d74c5 (''Financial Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**The death toll of [[dolphin]]s in [[Mauritius]] rises to 38, according to a [[government of Mauritius|government]] official. The dolphins showed signs of wounds but no trace of [[hydrocarbon]]s in their bodies. [[Greenpeace]] urged yesterday the government to launch an "urgent investigation to determine the cause of the deaths and any ties to the ''Wakashio'' oil spill". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mauritius-environment-dolphins/death-toll-of-mauritius-dolphins-is-now-38-government-official-idUSKBN25O1JA?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Officials in [[Niger]] say that floods have killed 45 people and displaced more than 226,000 people since Monday, after torrential rains caused the [[Niger River]] to overflow. Prime Minister [[Brigi Rafini]] pledges aid. [https://apnews.com/e60edb661c13c47d294c56cd57fc3e98 (AP)]
*A [[polar bear]] kills a 38-year-old Dutch man at campsite near [[Longyearbyen]], on the [[Arctic]] archipelago of [[Svalbard]]. The bear was then shot dead near [[Svalbard Airport, Longyear|Svalbard Airport]]. It is the first fatal bear attack on Svalbard since a British student was attacked and killed in 2011. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53945950 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] surpasses 100,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2020/08/michigan-surpasses-100000-confirmed-coronavirus-cases.html (MLive.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Canada]] extends emergency orders that place restrictions on international travel and make mandatory two-week quarantines for anyone entering the country until September 30. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7304292/coronavirus-canada-extending-international-travel-restrictions-mandatory-quarantine-until-sept-30/ (Global News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports more than 77,000 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total to more than 3.38 million, the highest single day spike for the country for the second consecutive day, and the highest single day caseload in the world apart from the [[United States]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/india-coronavirus-largest-daily-cases/2020/08/28/7cf61f0a-e7c1-11ea-bf44-0d31c85838a5_story.html?outputType (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports 3,003 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total to 165,887. This is a new record high for the second consecutive day since the pandemic began in the country. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5150417/update-corona-indonesia-28-agustus-rekor-3003-kasus-baru-total-165887 (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[Prime Minister of South Korea|Prime Minister]] [[Chung Sye-kyun]] announces that [[South Korea|the country]]'s level 2 restrictions, set to expire on August 30, would be extended for at least another week until September 6 as the [[Ministry of Health and Welfare (South Korea)|Ministry of Health and Welfare]] reports over 370 new infections over the past 24 hours. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/skorea-extends-covid-19-restrictions-as-virus-spikes/1955842 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The [[Minister of Health (France)|health ministry]] says that [[France]] is seeing an "exponential" rise in cases as the country records its second-highest record of reported cases since March, with 7,379 new cases in the last 24 hours, raising the possibility of another nationwide lockdown. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53954562 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****The [[Ministry of Citizen Protection (Greece)|Ministry of Citizen Protection]] announces changes to [[Greece]]'s [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic|travel restrictions]], effective August 31 until at least September 19, due to a rise in cases in recent weeks. Changes include requiring visitors from a list of countries to show a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test]] result to enter and a suspension of flights to and from [[Catalonia]], [[Spain]], but lifting restrictions on [[the Netherlands]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/greece-bans-flights-from-barcelona--extends-covid-19-travel-restrictions-13064106 (Reuters via CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] announces that it will close its borders to foreigners on September 1 in an attempt to curb a rise in infections, and Hungarians returning from abroad will have to go into two-week quarantine. Hungarians can only leave if they have provided two negative tests. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-hungary-borders/hungary-to-close-borders-to-foreigners-as-of-sept-1-to-curb-coronavirus-infections-idUSKBN25O273 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malawi]]
***The [[government of Malawi|government]] announces that the [[Lilongwe International Airport]] and [[Education in Malawi|all public schools in the country]] will reopen on September 1 and 7, respectively, following a reported significant decrease in new cases and deaths. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/covid-19-malawi-to-reopen-schools-sept-7/1955757 (Anadolu Agency)]

;International relations
*[[Norway–Russia relations]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian foreign ministry]] announces the expulsion of a senior diplomat at the [[Embassy of Norway in Moscow|Norwegian embassy]] in [[Moscow]] and declared him ''[[persona non grata]]'' as a "retaliatory measure" after the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Norway)|Norwegian foreign ministry]] had expelled the deputy trade representative of the [[Embassy of Russia in Oslo|Russian embassy]] in [[Oslo]] on August 19 for alleged espionage. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/08/28/russia-expels-norwegian-diplomat-in-spy-affair-a71270 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[European Union–Turkey relations]], [[Greece–Turkey relations]]
**Top [[European Union|EU]] diplomat [[Josep Borrell]] threatens [[Turkey]] with sanctions unless it and [[Greece]] reconcile their differences over maritime borders and gas drilling rights near [[Cyprus]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/eu-warns-turkey-sanctions-east-mediterranean-crisis-worsens-200828145842821.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**50,000 people gather in [[Washington, D.C.]] to commemorate the 1963 [[March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom|civil rights march]] and in protest against police violence. The event is called the "Commitment March: Get Your Knee Off Our Necks", a reference to [[Killing of George Floyd|George Floyd's killing]]. The relatives of [[Shooting of Jacob Blake|Jacob Blake]], [[George Floyd]], [[Shooting of Breonna Taylor|Breonna Taylor]], and [[Killing of Eric Garner|Eric Garner]] deliver speeches at the march alongside civil rights leaders [[Al Sharpton]] and [[Martin Luther King III]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53949460 (BBC News)]
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
**An [[administrative court]] in [[Berlin]] overturns the [[Government of Berlin|city government]]'s ban on protests and demonstrations, citing "no indication" that the government's rationale for the ban of protesters breaching [[Social distancing measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic#Germany|social distancing measures]] would occur. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/1976603/berlin-braces-for-anti-corona-demonstration (AFP via ''Bangkok Post'')]
*[[Essex lorry deaths]]
**A 40-year-old haulier from [[County Armagh]], [[Northern Ireland]], pleads guilty in the [[Old Bailey|Central Criminal Court of England and Wales]] to the [[Manslaughter in English law|manslaughter]] of 39 [[Vietnamese people]], as well as conspiring to assist [[Illegal immigration to the United Kingdom|unlawful immigration]]. [https://www.wellingtontimes.com.au/story/6900958/man-pleads-guilty-over-truck-deaths-in-uk/?cs=5461 (AAP via ''Wellington Times'')]
*[[Egypt]]ian authorities arrest Mahmoud Ezzat, the leader of the [[Muslim Brotherhood]]. He was serving a sentence ''[[Trial in absentia|in absentia]]'' and was detained in a hideout in [[Cairo]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/28/Egypt-arrests-Muslim-Brotherhood-leader-Mahmoud-Ezzat.html (Al Arabiya)]
*The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights]] [[Michelle Bachelet]] says that the life of top [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] doctor [[Denis Mukwege]], a [[Nobel Peace Prize]] winner, is "at serious risk" after receiving multiple death threats via phone calls and social media. His hospital is located in the middle of a conflict zone and the Congolese government pledged to protect him after he survived an [[assassination]] attempt years ago. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security-doctor/u-n-says-life-of-congos-nobel-laureate-doctor-in-danger-idUSKBN25O1V4?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A [[Pakistan]]i court sentences three leaders of [[Lashkar-e-Taiba|Jamat-ud-Dawa]] to between one and 16 years in prison for helping coordinate the [[2008 Mumbai attacks]]. The sentences come as the deadline for the country to avoid getting placed on the [[Financial Action Task Force]] blacklist approaches. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-court-fatf/pakistan-jails-three-accused-of-financing-mumbai-attacks-idUSKBN25O2OI?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Rioting erupts in [[Malmö]], [[Sweden]], following a [[Quran]] [[book burning]] event by far-right Danish politician [[Rasmus Paludan]] in the city. Police say as many as 300 people gathered to protest the anti-Islam activities, which then became violent as protesters set fires and attacked police. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-sweden-riot/violence-erupts-in-swedish-town-of-malmo-after-anti-islam-actions-police-say-idUKKBN25O31L?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Brazilian Ministry of Health]] announces expansions to [[Abortion in Brazil|the country's abortion laws]] regarding cases of [[pregnancy from rape]], which include requiring the victim to provide "a detailed account" to doctors, a report to [[Federal Police of Brazil|police]], and the victim being "expressly warned" of the possibility of prosecution for fraud for false or unverified claims. [[Chamber of Deputies (Brazil)|Chamber of Deputies]] minority leader [[Jandira Feghali]] filed a bill in response to block the decree, claiming it "constitutes [[Psychological abuse|psychological violence]] [[Violence against women|against women]]". [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/americas/brazil-expands-requirements-for-abortion-in-rape-cases (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Prime Minister of Japan|Japanese Prime Minister]] [[Shinzō Abe]] announces his intention to resign due to his deteriorating health. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/28/asia/shinzo-abe-japan-resignation-health-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)] [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/08/49143d2e31c6-breaking-news-abes-health-status-remains-unchanged-top-govt-spokesman.html (Kyodo News)]
*[[Prime Minister of Libya]] [[Fayez al-Sarraj]], of the [[Government of National Accord]] in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], suspends [[Ministry of Interior (Libya)|Minister of Interior]] [[Fathi Bashagha]] from duties. Sarraj says Bashaga will be investigated over a violent crackdown on street protests. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/influential-libyan-interior-minister-suspended-amid-protests-idUSKBN25O301 (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*American [[neurotechnology]] company [[Neuralink]] unveils a [[pig]], named "Gertrude", that has been living with a [[Brain implant|brain-implanted chip]] for two months at an event in [[San Francisco]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tech-neuralink-musk/three-little-pigs-musks-neuralink-puts-computer-chips-in-animal-brains-idUSKBN25O2EG?il=0 (Reuters)]
